title: Three Rivers Cook Book, with Supplement
about: A reprint published by the King’s Daughters Society of Three Rivers, a church women’s service circle, with recipes signed by the women of the town and advertisements from its shops. Digitized by Michigan State University Libraries.

title: New Crumbs of Comfort
about: Compiled by the ladies of St. Luke’s Church, Kalamazoo, with nearly two hundred pages of signed recipes, household hints and local advertising. Library of Congress copy, on the Internet Archive.

title: Michigan State Federation Cook Book
about: Gathered from members of women’s clubs across Michigan and edited by Sarah Marshall Weaver. Every recipe is signed with the cook’s name and town, which is how cooks from Dowagiac, Cassopolis, Marcellus, Three Rivers, Constantine, Sturgis, St. Joseph, Benton Harbor, Paw Paw and Bangor appear in it.

title: The Inglenook Cook Book
about: About a thousand numbered recipes sent in by women of the Church of the Brethren. The strong Brethren congregations of northern Indiana put cooks from Goshen, Nappanee, South Bend and Walkerton in its pages, with Pennsylvania Dutch dishes such as buttermilk delda and boiled potpie.

title: The Evening News, Benton Harbor
about: Benton Harbor’s daily paper. For Christmas 1897 it ran a contest for a holiday dinner costing $2.00, printing readers’ menus with every item priced and the cook’s own recipes.

title: Dr. Miles’ Candy Book
about: A giveaway booklet from the Dr. Miles Medical Company of Elkhart, makers of Dr. Miles’ Nervine: home candy recipes on one page, patent-medicine advertising on the next.

title: South Bend News-Times
about: South Bend’s daily paper, which ran a “Canning Lesson” column in the wartime fall of 1917. Read on Hoosier State Chronicles, the Indiana State Library’s newspaper archive.

title: Nappanee Advance-News
about: The weekly paper of Nappanee, in Elkhart County, with household advice for farm kitchens. Read on Hoosier State Chronicles.
